licenseeAdmin.scope: PolicyAlert.licenseeId must equal the database-verified canonical licensee for an active LICENSEE_ADMIN or ORG_ADMIN actor.

manufacturer.scope: PolicyAlert.manufacturerId must equal the database-verified manufacturer actor; any batch or QR reference must independently resolve to that actor and one active linked licensee.

public.reason: No registered product route has an unguessable proof-bound, non-enumerable public alert projection.

requiredAssurance.manufacturerAlertRead: password-verified active session for the future safe-summary projection; any future mutation requires separately approved MFA
requiredAssurance.incidentResponseAlertRead: step-up-verified plus active incident authorization expiring within 60 minutes
requiredAssurance.alertEscalation: step-up-verified plus active incident authorization expiring within 60 minutes

scopeModels.policyAlertTerminal: PolicyAlert.licenseeId is mandatory and is the terminal tenant boundary. NULL or blank is invalid and never global.
scopeModels.policyRuleParent: When policyRuleId is present, PolicyRule.licenseeId must equal PolicyAlert.licenseeId; an organization-scoped rule must resolve to the same Licensee.organization, and a manufacturer rule must also match manufacturerId.
scopeModels.batchParent: When batchId is present, Batch.licenseeId must equal PolicyAlert.licenseeId; if manufacturerId is present, Batch.manufacturerId must equal it.
scopeModels.qrParent: When qrCodeId is present, QRCode.licenseeId and QRCode.batch.licenseeId must equal PolicyAlert.licenseeId; a manufacturer actor must own the referenced batch.
scopeModels.incidentParent: When incidentId is present, Incident.licenseeId must be non-NULL and equal PolicyAlert.licenseeId; incident authorization is an additional ceiling, never a replacement for tenant scope.
scopeModels.manufacturerActor: When manufacturerId is present, it must identify the active manufacturer User and equal app.manufacturer_id for manufacturer reads; the active Licensee and Organization and a ManufacturerLicenseeLink row must agree.
scopeModels.platformOnlySecurityEvent: SecurityEventOutbox rows are system-owned delivery records. JSON payload scope is not authority and must be revalidated from authoritative identifiers before delivery.
scopeModels.ambiguousOrMultiParent: All non-NULL parents must resolve to one licensee and consistent manufacturer. Any conflict, missing parent, disabled tenant, or ambiguous relationship fails closed.

terminalAuthorizationBoundaries.terminalBoundary: exact manufacturer actor plus one verified linked licensee
one database-validated licensee, manufacturer, batch, QR, actor, or alert selector under platform-read-scope-v1
one active incident authorization plus its exact licensee
exact alert ID under canonical licensee
exact alert and exact active incident sharing one licensee
exact tenant and incident arguments under operator-boundary-tenant-incident-summary

nestedProjectionRules.displayNames: Only an approved licensee, rule, batch, or actor display name may be joined; email, prefix, code payload, and security state are omitted.

lifecycleTransitions.sourceState: acknowledgedAt IS NULL AND acknowledgedByUserId IS NULL
lifecycleTransitions.targetState: acknowledgedAt IS NOT NULL AND acknowledgedByUserId = verified actor
lifecycleTransitions.concurrency: database compare-and-set on id, canonical licenseeId, acknowledgedAt IS NULL, and acknowledgedByUserId IS NULL; exactly one row may change
lifecycleTransitions.idempotency: A replay with the same idempotency key and actor returns the original acknowledgement; a conflicting actor, scope, or payload is denied.
lifecycleTransitions.replay: Clearing acknowledgement is prohibited. Zero-row CAS reloads the scoped row and returns the existing result only for a matching replay.
lifecycleTransitions.approvalRequirement: none beyond actor ceiling and MFA
lifecycleTransitions.notificationSideEffects: Tenant-safe notification is enqueued after the transition in the same transaction/outbox boundary; no email, raw payload, or foreign scope.

lifecycleTransitions.targetState: incidentId = exact active incident ID sharing PolicyAlert.licenseeId
lifecycleTransitions.concurrency: database compare-and-set on alert id, canonical licenseeId, and incidentId IS NULL after locking or validating the exact incident in the same transaction
lifecycleTransitions.idempotency: A matching replay may return the existing incident link; a different incident ID is a conflict and is denied.
lifecycleTransitions.replay: Unlinking or reassigning an incident is prohibited without a separately approved lifecycle.
lifecycleTransitions.approvalRequirement: active incident authorization plus step-up; operator procedure if durable incident authorization is unavailable
lifecycleTransitions.notificationSideEffects: Only incident-scoped redacted notifications are emitted after commit through an approved outbox.

lifecycleTransitions.concurrency: no transition permitted because PolicyAlert has no assignment state or version
lifecycleTransitions.approvalRequirement: new product and schema decision required

lifecycleTransitions.concurrency: no transition permitted because PolicyAlert has no resolution status, resolvedAt, reason, version, or immutable transition record
lifecycleTransitions.approvalRequirement: new product and schema decision required

lifecycleTransitions.concurrency: no transition permitted because PolicyAlert has no suppression status, expiry, reason, approver, or version
lifecycleTransitions.approvalRequirement: new product and schema decision required

concurrencyRules.deterministicConcurrentLoser: matching replay returns the original result; conflicting transition returns conflict without mutation

idempotencyReplaySemantics.scope: actor ID + canonical licensee + alert ID + action class

approvalRequirements.tenantRead: none beyond verified actor, scope, MFA, purpose, and attribution
approvalRequirements.manufacturerRead: none beyond verified actor, exact own-object scope, purpose, and attribution
approvalRequirements.incidentReadOrEscalation: active expiring incident authorization; use operator-boundary-tenant-incident-summary if unavailable

workflowClassifications.scopeRule: PolicyAlert.licenseeId must equal the active LICENSEE_ADMIN or ORG_ADMIN actor's database-verified canonical licensee. Platform and manufacturer actors are denied on this route.
blockers: The current route lacks recent MFA, fixed purpose, request attribution, date/keyset bounds, transaction-client-only access, explicit select, and same-snapshot count/list; platform role currently reaches a blank-scope fallback.

workflowClassifications.scopeRule: The exact alert ID must resolve under the active tenant administrator's canonical licensee; platform and manufacturer actors are denied on this route.
blockers: The current controller performs a pre-check plus unconditional update, has no database CAS/idempotency record, returns the full row, and writes audit/notifications outside one canonical transaction.

workflowClassifications.scopeRule: Every alert must match an active unexpired incident authorization and its exact licensee; optional alert, batch, QR, manufacturer, rule, type, severity, or acknowledgement filters only narrow that set.
blockers: The product has no durable expiring incident-read authorization. The current route lacks recent MFA, incident binding, purpose, attribution, explicit select, keyset/date bounds, same transaction, and redacts neither nested emails nor raw alert details.

workflowClassifications.scopeRule: The exact alert and exact active incident must share one licensee and fall under one unexpired incident authorization; acknowledgement, unlinking, reassignment, and mixed-field patch requests are denied on this workflow.
blockers: The current generic patch accepts acknowledgement toggles and incident unlinking, does not validate incident tenant/authorization, lacks reason, request ID, purpose, CAS/idempotency, and atomic audit/outbox behavior. Split or narrow the route before implementation.

workflowClassifications.scopeRule: The identity-worker runtime may claim only an allowlisted durable SecurityEventOutbox row under worker-boundary-siem-outbox-delivery; JSON scope never establishes tenant or human authority.
blockers: The governing worker contract is approved, but runtime still needs durable payload digest/scope fields, per-row database claim, maximum-attempt dead-letter behavior, secret-free event schemas, and PostgreSQL certification.

inspectedButNotGovernedWorkflows.reason: Already governed by the implemented bounded fraud-report read contract; it is not a PolicyAlert lifecycle and remains pending PostgreSQL certification.
Append-only AuditLog response semantics are not PolicyAlert state; it remains blocked pending bounded scope, fixed purpose, unique transition/idempotency, and atomic attribution.
Mixed incident, alert, print, support, audit, tenant, manufacturer, and platform roots must split before the alert slice can use manufacturer-alert-read; current platform blank scope remains blocked.
Alert generation is a separate system/lifecycle write boundary, not a human actor read or lifecycle action classified by this decision.
Generic notification creation mixes alert and non-alert producers and must be split by owning transaction before an alert delivery contract can be attached.
Incident lifecycle notification is governed by the incident transaction and notification visibility contract, not direct PolicyAlert access.

allowScenarios: A database-verified active licensee administrator with fresh MFA, request ID, tenant-alert-review purpose, and canonical licensee reads at most 100 projected alerts for that licensee in one attributed transaction.
A database-verified active licensee administrator acknowledges one unacknowledged alert in their licensee through a one-row CAS and same-transaction immutable attribution.
A platform incident responder with step-up assurance and an active unexpired incident authorization reads only projected alerts bound to that incident and licensee.
An incident responder links one unlinked alert to one same-licensee incident through a one-row CAS, reason, idempotency key, immutable attribution, and approved outbox.
The identity-worker runtime delivers one allowlisted durable outbox event through worker-boundary-siem-outbox-delivery without installing human context.
denyScenarios: Generic admin, role text alone, password-only sensitive administration, missing purpose/request ID, blank or foreign scope, NULL or conflicting parents, stale assurance, or platform-wide fallback is denied.
A manufacturer cannot read all alerts for a linked licensee; no current workflow is approved for manufacturer alert details.
Assignment, PolicyAlert resolution, suppression, unacknowledgement, incident unlinking, incident reassignment, mixed acknowledgement/escalation patch, or protected ownership changes are denied.
Raw details, secret indicators, personal data, full network/device fingerprints, raw audit data, SIEM credentials, or unrelated tenant identifiers are denied.
Public access is denied; no alert ID, tenant reference, signed QR reference, or notification token currently proves a public alert disclosure.
Workers cannot impersonate humans and operators cannot replace exact procedures with direct alert-table access.

crossReferences.publicReadContract: public-read-contract-v1 classifies every alert disclosure as prohibited-public-access; no signed scan, support proof, public reference or notification token authorizes PolicyAlert or incident-security detail.

postgresqlCertificationRequirements: Prove tenant own-scope allow and foreign/blank/NULL/ambiguous scope denial for PolicyAlert SELECT and UPDATE.
Prove platform role alone and missing/stale MFA, purpose, request ID, incident ID, authorization, or expiry denial.
Prove manufacturer actor scope cannot expand to all alerts for a linked licensee.
Prove SELECT projection excludes details and every prohibited or nested secret-bearing field.
Prove acknowledgement and escalation use database-enforced one-row CAS with deterministic replay and protected ownership columns.
Prove assignment, resolution, suppression, unacknowledgement, unlinking, reassignment, public access, and mixed patch are denied.
Prove count/list scope and snapshot match and immutable read/mutation attribution shares the transaction.
Prove worker delivery uses identity-worker, durable row authority, row claim, idempotency, bounded retries, and no human context.
Prove operator incident summaries are executable only through operator-boundary-tenant-incident-summary.
Retain all four currently pending workflow certifications until disposable PostgreSQL evidence is reviewed.
